intro1.say: Meet Sentiment Interpreter, a live interpreter that keeps the feeling, not just the words.
intro1.cap: Meet Sentiment Interpreter: it keeps the feeling, not just the words.

intro2.say: Choose how you talk to it, by voice or by text, and how you hear it back.
intro2.cap: Talk to it by voice or by text, and hear or read it back.

text.say: First, typing. A warm little thank-you, with a tilde and an emoji.
text.cap: First, typing: a warm little thank-you, with ~ and 😊.

textAfter.say: The aww, the tilde and the smile all come through, in a warm Korean voice.
textAfter.cap: The “aww”, the ~ and the smile all come through, in a warm Korean voice.

voice.say: Now speech. Here's German, with doch mal.
voice.cap: Now speech: German, with doch mal.

voiceAfter.say: The casual, inviting tone stays casual in Korean.
voiceAfter.cap: The casual, inviting tone stays casual in Korean.

pace.say: Pace sets how quickly it translates after you pause.
pace.cap: Pace sets how quickly it translates after you pause.

meeting.say: Meeting mode puts live subtitles on screen. In Chrome, they float above your slides or video call.
meeting.cap: Meeting mode: live subtitles that float above your slides or video call.

meetingAfter.say: Speak in short chunks, and the subtitles keep up.
meetingAfter.cap: Speak in short chunks, and the subtitles keep up.

rubric.say: Every translation is guided by the same rubric as Sentiment Translator: sentiment, formality and friendliness.
rubric.cap: Guided by the SFF rubric: sentiment, formality and friendliness.

outro.say: Built on the Gemini Live API, and redesigned with Claude Code. Thanks for watching!
outro.cap: Built on the Gemini Live API, redesigned with Claude Code. Thanks for watching!
